w10_T4_005444: A fruit wholesaler unloaded 176 boxes of apples at the depot, and every box held 7 apples. Sorting found 73 apples bruised, and those went to the cider press instead. A late crate added 10 more apples to the pile. The kitchen then cut every apple in the pile into 3 slices for the school lunches, so the count tripled. How many apple slices went to the schools?
w10_T4_005454: Mira printed 55 large sheets for the fairground, and each sheet was perforated into 4 ride tickets. She and her colleague Sten divided the tickets equally among the 4 stalls, and Mira kept the batch for the gate stall while Sten took the rest. Every ticket in her batch is good for 7 rides on the carousel. Over the weekend riders used up 235 of those rides. Each ride still unused is worth 3 loyalty points, and the fair added 45 bonus points to Mira's card. How many loyalty points did Mira have?
w10_T4_005460: The bakery opened the morning with 99 trays, and each tray carried 9 bread rolls, with all baking times written in minutes rather than in hours. Before noon 472 rolls were sold at the counter. A second bake added 21 rolls to the racks. During the afternoon the rolls were shared equally among the 5 shops in the group, and the driver stayed with the delivery for the Elm Street shop. In the evening that shop sold 21 rolls to a restaurant. How many rolls did the Elm Street shop have left?
w10_T4_005462: The flower stall opened with 224 bunches of daffodils on the trestle. A wedding order took 220 bunches in one go before eight o'clock. The grower cut 24 more bunches and brought them down from the field. Rosa runs the stall with her brother Aleks, and she sold rather more than he did that day. Just 1 bunch wilted in the sun and was thrown out, and 9 further bunches were sold to passing customers. How many bunches were left on the trestle?
w10_T4_005464: Bo filled 114 crates at the cider press, and every crate holds 3 bottles. His partner Ida, whose smaller press had produced less, added 22 bottles of her own. At the autumn fair 267 bottles were sold from the stall. A village pub then bought 46 bottles for its beer festival. Bo brought up 40 more bottles from the cellar to restock. How many bottles did they have?
w10_T4_005465: The brickworks had 214 pallets in the yard when the gates opened, and each pallet was stacked with 8 boxes. Every box on those pallets holds 7 bricks. Half of the yard is under cover. A storeman found 32 loose bricks by the kiln and added them to the tally. During the afternoon 7828 bricks went out to the housing site. In the evening every brick still in the yard was split cleanly in two for the decorative wall, giving twice as many pieces. How many pieces were in the yard?
w10_T4_005469: The garden centre has 208 display racks, and every rack holds 7 seed trays. Weekend customers bought 473 trays over two busy days. A grower delivered 76 more trays on the Monday. A landscaping firm then took 838 trays for a park contract. A school returned 53 trays it had ordered by mistake. Each tray still at the centre is planted with 5 young plants. How many young plants are at the garden centre?
w10_T4_005479: Kemal cut 173 lengths of leather at his bench, and each length yields 5 straps. His colleague Deniz, whose output was smaller that week, handed over 21 finished straps. Half of the straps are dyed black. The bag orders used up 695 straps before the end of the month. Kemal found 13 straps among his offcuts and bought 31 more from a tannery. Every strap still on the rack needs 3 rivets before it can be sold. How many rivets does the rack need?
w10_T4_005481: The conference centre has 58 meeting rooms, and each room is set out with 8 chairs. The building is 6 years old. The store cupboard supplied 62 extra chairs for the busiest day. Every chair in the centre was occupied for 3 separate sessions during the week. Each session gave its occupant 7 printed handouts. Delegates took 9053 of the handouts away with them. How many handouts were left behind in the rooms?
w10_T4_005490: The dairy depot counted 222 crates of milk in the chill room in the morning, and it prints its volumes in millilitres rather than in litres. The first round delivered 175 crates to the shops. The dairy sent up 60 fresh crates, a cafe returned 11 empties that were counted back in, and the second run brought back 70 crates. A dozen drivers work out of the yard. During the afternoon the crates were shared equally among the 4 village shops, and the supervisor followed the load for Ashby. In the evening 68 further crates were delivered to Ashby. How many crates did the Ashby shop have?
w10_T4_005497: The jamboree field held 235 tents when the gates opened in the morning. Groups leaving early took down 35 of them before nine o'clock. A gale damaged 17 more tents beyond use during the middle of the day. The quartermaster put up 13 replacement tents in the afternoon. Every tent standing on the field sleeps 6 scouts. In the evening the caterers worked out that each sleeping place needs 3 meals over the weekend. How many meals must the caterers prepare?
w10_T4_005499: The helpline recorded 87 calls before nine o'clock, and it logs every call length in seconds rather than in minutes. Another 14 calls came through during the middle of the morning, and 7 more over the lunch hour. Half of the callers ask about the same thing. The early afternoon brought 25 calls, and 26 more came in before the shift change. During the evening the team took a further 33 calls. How many calls did the helpline record that day?
w10_T4_005507: Rui counted 240 empty bottles at the recycling point when he arrived in the morning. His colleague Sara, whose van had collected more than his that week, unloaded 25 bottles, and a cafe left 28 by the gate. Each bottle handed in is worth 4 deposit tokens. During the afternoon 691 tokens were redeemed by people at the kiosk. In the evening a school collection brought in 72 more tokens, and a walker handed over 8 tokens he had found. How many tokens did the recycling point hold?
w10_T4_005510: The gym issued 210 day passes in the first week of January, and a promotion doubled the number issued so twice as many were in circulation. Ana, the manager, gave out 39 more to staff, rather more than her deputy Bram had handed out. The pool is 25 metres long, and sessions there are booked in minutes rather than in hours. An audit found 90 of the passes had expired and cancelled them. Every valid pass entitles its holder to 5 visits, and members have already used 519 visits. How many visits are still available?
w10_T4_005513: The village cafe had 31 cakes on its stand at opening, and the baker brought out 30 more during the morning. Every cake was cut in half for the tasting event, so the number of pieces doubled. The pieces were then shared equally between the 2 serving counters, and the owner kept an eye only on the window counter. The kitchen sent out 40 more pieces to that counter later on. How many pieces were on the window counter?
w10_T4_005514: The joinery had 116 planks in its rack and took delivery of 9 more, and it quotes plank thickness in millimetres rather than in centimetres. The planks were divided equally among the 5 work benches, and the foreman watched only the bench by the window. The building itself is 40 years old. Exactly 1 plank at that bench split along the grain and was discarded. Every remaining plank there was ripped into 3 slats, and each slat needs 5 nails to fix it. The joiner also had 31 spare nails in his apron. How many nails were at that bench?
w10_T4_005525: The garden pond started the spring with 15 water lilies. The gardener lifted out 8 of them because they had crowded the edge. Every lily left in the water sent out 5 new shoots by June. The gardener planted 37 further shoots from a nursery tray and was given 20 more by a neighbour. The pond measures 9 metres across at its widest. Each shoot opened 2 flowers that summer, twice what the older plants had managed. How many flowers opened on the pond?
w10_T4_005528: Iris had 26 photo frames in her studio cupboard. Her assistant Ben, whose own store was smaller, passed her 6 frames from the back room, and she bought 57 more at a closing-down sale. The studio charges 30 an hour for portrait sittings. Every frame in the cupboard holds 2 pictures behind its glass. Each picture was then scanned into 7 digital files for the archive. How many digital files were created?
w10_T4_005533: Otto baked 203 loaves for the harvest supper, and his partner Vera, who had spent the day on the puddings, contributed 12 loaves of her own. Every loaf was cut into 7 thick slices for the long tables. A spare loaf from the kitchen produced 42 further slices, which went onto the same platters. Each slice was served with 2 pats of butter. How many pats of butter were served?
w10_T4_005534: The sports club started the year with 231 footballs in its store. It sent 205 of them out to primary schools in the district. The main pitch is 100 metres long. Lena donated 72 balls after a fundraiser, more than Marc managed to collect with his sponsored run, and the club bought 80 more with the proceeds. Over the season 45 balls were lost over the fence and 82 were given to a partner club in the next county. A dozen coaches work with the junior teams, and one of them found 7 balls in an old kit bag. How many footballs were in the store?
w10_T4_005544: The cable factory had 165 drums in its store and took in 77 more from the drawing shop. Every drum carries 8 coils of copper cable. Each coil was cut in half for the transport contract, so the number of pieces doubled. The factory runs 3 shifts a day. A technician added 9 spare pieces from the test rig to the batch. Every piece needs 6 connectors before it can be installed, and the contract used up 21233 connectors. How many connectors were left in the store?
w10_T4_005549: Amir had 114 blank keycards for the new building, and the system logs access times in minutes rather than in hours. His colleague Ruth, who had ordered more than he had, gave him 68 cards from her own box. Testing showed 31 of the cards to be faulty and they were destroyed. Every working card is programmed to open 9 doors in the complex. The security review then revoked 26 of those door permissions. How many door permissions were active?
w10_T4_005560: Ines ordered 164 sheets of glass for the conservatory job, and her partner Karl, whose order had been smaller, added 32 sheets from his own stock. Every sheet was scored and cut into 6 panes. The glazier found 32 spare panes in the racks and counted them with the rest. The greenhouse repair swallowed 440 panes over two weeks. Every pane still in the workshop needs 3 metal clips to hold it in a frame, and there were 36 loose clips in the drawer as well. How many clips were in the workshop?
w10_T4_005565: The stationer had 39 boxes of chalk on the shelf at the start of term, and the shop has been trading for 11 years. A local school bought 35 of the boxes in one order. A wholesaler then delivered 76 boxes, and a closing college donated 21 more. Half of the chalk in stock is white. Over the term 87 boxes were sold across the counter. The remaining boxes were divided equally between 2 classrooms, and the caretaker carried one classroom's share upstairs. How many boxes went upstairs?
w10_T4_005568: The school planted 33 tomato plants in its polytunnel in the spring. A cold snap in May killed 15 of them before they flowered. Every plant that survived carried 6 trusses by the middle of the summer. Each truss ripened 5 tomatoes for the cookery lessons. The gardening club saved 5 seeds from every tomato for the following year. How many seeds did the club save?
